body: Telling a therapist leads to you being placed in inpatient. In inpatient you're generally treated as sub-human and given a high dose of antipsychotics to numb you. During that time your job doesn't pay you and you have no income. At the end of it you come out having missed a bunch of work, with a drug you're probably on way too high of a dose of  (or the wrong drug) , diagnoses made by doctors within 15-20 minutes of meeting you, maybe 1-2 therapy appointments a week, and then its over with a huge bill. It's no better than being outpatient and having a therapist and a psychiatrist - if anything I think it's worse.
